title: What If Smallpox Had Never Been Eradicated?

scenes.text: What if smallpox was never eradicated? It killed 300 million people last century.
About three in ten people who caught it died, according to the CDC and NIAID.
In 1967, the World Health Organization launched an intensified push to wipe it out.
The last natural case was a hospital cook in Somalia, in October 1977.
In 1980, the World Health Assembly declared smallpox eradicated, the first human disease ever wiped out.
Without that campaign, it could still be circulating today. Instead, it took just ten years to end.

description:
What if smallpox had never been eradicated?
It killed an estimated 300 million people in the twentieth century, until a vaccination campaign ended it in 1980.
